rules.explanation: Creating a repository matching your username activates a special Profile README that acts as a developer landing page for visiting tech leads and recruiters.
rules.do: Include a brief intro, technical stack badges, current project focus, contact links, and dynamic GitHub stats widgets.
rules.dont: Do not leave the special profile repository uncreated or filled only with default template placeholders.

rules.explanation: GitHub allows pinning up to 6 key repositories on your main profile. These represent your highest engineering standards to anyone visiting your account.
rules.do: Pin your 4 to 6 best repositories that have full documentation, clean code, tests, and active commits.
rules.dont: Do not pin empty repositories, old high school hello-world tests, or fork-only repositories with no original code.

rules.rule_name: Consistent Commit Activity and Green Graph
rules.explanation: A steady contribution graph signals continuous learning, discipline, and regular engagement with version control systems.
rules.do: Maintain steady, authentic coding activity across open-source contributions, personal projects, or private work graphs.
rules.dont: Do not go dormant for months at a time or rely on fake commit-generator scripts to pad the contribution matrix.

rules.rule_name: Active Open Source and Public Engagement
rules.explanation: Contributing pull requests, reporting issues, or reviewing code in community repositories demonstrates collaboration readiness.
rules.do: Participate in open-source discussions, issue triage, or pull requests in relevant industry tools/frameworks.
rules.dont: Do not treat GitHub purely as a passive cloud backup drive without utilizing its collaborative social features.
